_what: The one source of the three pathway definitions shown under BUILD, GROW and LAUNCH on the education front door. The renderer reads this file and refuses to build if it is malformed, empty or names a placement instrument; the check reads the same file, so the band and the record cannot drift.
_ruling: D-3, docs/orders/SERVED_DEFECTS_AMENDMENT_2026-09-16.md (Lessons). Raised by Matt on 16 September 2026 from the served page; source supplied by Matt.
_source: Progress Schools Curriculum Policy 2026/27, Issue 2, section 5.3 Pathways, read with section 3.2 (stage-not-age). Each definition is a faithful compression of its section 5.3 paragraph.
_constraint: Public copy describes what a pathway OFFERS, never how a student is scored into it. Section 5.3 and section 6 name placement instruments and assessment data; none may appear here, in any form (R11). No product name (R10).
_scope: Section 5.3 describes four pathways. Reintegration is a time-limited commissioned placement aligned to a home school, not a teaching pathway with lessons on this estate, so the band stays at three by design.

pathways.name: BUILD
pathways.definition: For students who are not yet consistently ready for formal learning. Short, calm learning episodes with strong visual and communication support, building reading readiness, confidence and small-step achievements.

pathways.name: GROW
pathways.definition: The bridge between nurture and formal learning. Practical, real-world tasks that build everyday reading, writing and number, applied subject learning and a portfolio of evidence.

pathways.name: LAUNCH
pathways.definition: For students ready for formal qualifications with therapeutic support in place. Exam readiness, revision routines, access arrangements and planning for life after school.
